note: VERIFIED BY ORCHA — the P1 differential metric is measuring the wrong thing. src/differential.zig groupByResult() keys boards by a hash of OUTPUT VALUES; compare() then labels the largest value-group 'agreements' and every other value-group a 'disagreement'. It never compares implementations to each other. 'area_score 2x2: 19/81, 6 disagreements' means 19 boards share the modal score and 7 distinct scores exist (19 + six other groups = 81). exp6.genericAreaScore and Rules(w,h).area_score are line-for-line identical INCLUDING their neighbour functions; they agree on all 81 and all 729 boards. Correct metric: per board, evaluate every impl, count boards where all results are equal; a disagreement is a board where they differ, reported with each impl's differing value. Your TDD fixture passed because it only asserted that more than one group appears — it cannot distinguish 'impls disagree' from 'outputs vary'. That is the broken-positive-control class already on record as CODE.M4A-HARNESS's A6 fixture: a control that passes for the wrong reason. Fix the metric, re-run, and treat the first matrix as not yet taken.

STANDING REQUIREMENT for every instrument this sprint builds or touches — red-green-refactor applied to the instruments themselves (Beck TDD; maxim: never trust a test you haven't seen fail). Before an instrument's first real reading is believed it must pass BOTH controls: (1) NULL CONTROL — give it the same implementation twice; it must report perfect agreement. Today's harness fails this instantly and nobody ran it. (2) SEEDED-DEFECT CONTROL — register a deliberately mutated copy of a real implementation (flip a comparison, change a constant, swap an argument); the instrument must report it as a disagreement, naming the witness inputs. A positive control alone is not enough: this harness's known-bad fixture passed for the wrong reason, because groupByResult produces multiple groups whenever OUTPUTS vary. Same defect class as CODE.M4A-HARNESS's A6 fixture. NOTE THE LEVERAGE: a mutant is just another implementation, so the differential harness IS a mutation-testing rig (DeMillo/Lipton/Sayward 1978) at no extra cost. Registering mutants as implementations gives a mutation score — the percentage of injected faults the comparison catches — which is a measured answer to 'can our checks ever go red'. Build it that way rather than as a one-off fix. SECOND ITEM: sort the duplicate implementations into CLONES and INDEPENDENTS before counting oracle value. exp6.genericAreaScore and Rules.area_score are line-for-line identical including neighbour functions — that is copy-paste, and clones cannot catch each other's errors. Only uncorrelated origins count as oracles: the Python reference, exp4 vs exp6 as different generations, the tested core vs the solvers. Report the two categories separately; agreement among clones is worth nothing and must not be reported as reassurance.

FOUR REFINEMENTS from the Orchestrator, after the operator pushed back. (1) MY PIGEONHOLE CORRECTION IN THE BRIEF WAS BESIDE THE POINT AND THE OPERATOR IS RIGHT. Infinite play must repeat, but ARBITRARILY LONG FINITE play need not: a game can run hundreds of plies of clump-die-clump-die, late-game to early-game and back many times, without ever repeating a position exactly, because 3^16 is about 43 million positions and the walk never has to close a loop. The consequence is the important part and it reorders the project's options: POSITIONAL SUPERKO DOES NOT PREVENT THIS. PSK forbids repetition, and these absurd games do not repeat, so PSK would still admit them and would still let them determine values. Only a material or progress rule rules them out. Record this explicitly — it means the capture budget is attacking something PSK structurally cannot reach, and it raises this row's value relative to T386. (2) THE KEY-GROWTH QUESTION THE OPERATOR ASKED IS THE REAL DESIGN FORK, AND THEY SPOTTED IT. Two designs, and they are not equivalent. (a) BUDGET IN THE KEY: captures-so-far becomes part of the state, key grows by B+1, and V(P,c) relates to V(child,c+captured) — BELLMAN-CONSISTENT, which is what the whole verification battery rests on (I4 checks exactly this residual). (b) BUDGET FROM HERE, which is what the operator proposes for Pass 3: each bracketed position is resolved by its own bounded forward search counting captures from itself, no key growth, much cheaper. But (b) IS NOT BELLMAN-CONSISTENT BY CONSTRUCTION: P's value computed with a budget counted from P need not equal the max/min over its children's values each computed with a budget counted from themselves, so the resulting table can fail the very identity T343 verified at 0/95,677,624. MEASURE THE INCONSISTENCY RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT IS FATAL — resolve the 3x3 bracketed set both ways and report Bellman residual violations for each, with denominators. If (b)'s residual is 0 or tiny and explainable, it is the cheap winner; if it is large, (a) is the honest design and its B+1 cost is the price. This comparison is now the row's central deliverable. (3) 'CAPTURES BECOME ILLEGAL' IS MY WORDING AND IT IS DEGENERATE — the operator's original 'then the game ends' is cleaner and should be the primary variant. If captures merely become illegal, dead stones can never be removed and an opponent can fill your established territory with unremovable stones and steal area under area scoring. Terminating the game at the budget and scoring as-it-stands has no such hole. Test 'terminate and score' as variant 1 and 'captures illegal' as variant 2, and expect the second to show the degeneracy. (4) OPERATOR'S PRIOR: B = 8 at 4x4, half the board's points, chosen to break the full-board cycle. Sweep around it rather than only at it, and run the SAME instrument at every size — 3x3, 4x3, 4x4 — since the operator's standing methodological point is that a result at one size is a hypothesis for every other, so the test must be size-parametric by construction. Skip 2x2; the operator considers it uninteresting.

CLARIFICATION OF THE OPERATOR'S DESIGN (b) — the Orchestrator explained it back wrongly and the correct version is cheaper than either variant in your brief. The operator's proposal, in their words 2026-08-06: from a bracketed position P, play ALL possible games forward as a tree whose nodes REMEMBER THE CAPTURES SO FAR, up to max X captured stones, and let the finisher choose optimal paths P->terminal. They then identified the real constraint themselves: they want Bellman/memoisation so forward nodes can be RECYCLED across different bracketed roots and across branches of the same search. That recycling is what forces the design, and here is the resolution: the capture counter belongs in the SEARCH MEMO KEY, not in the persistent table key. A node reached from root P1 with c=3 is a genuinely different memo entry from the same position reached from P2 with c=1, so the memo key is (colex, side, ko, passes, c) — but the persistent WZO2 table keeps its existing key and never grows. COST, which is the point: (X+1) x THE TANGLED REGION rather than (B+1) x the whole table.
